title: The Reckoning
subtitle: Sunday 11 to Saturday 24 December 1864: A Warrant for Fiddler's, Deadfall Canyon from the Top, the Last Coach, Fire in the Snow, and Christmas Eve

setting.name: The Bannack road, Fiddler's Station, Deadfall Canyon and Ninebark, the last two weeks of 1864
setting.description: The party has warrants, and Warrick Sefton has a plan. On Thursday 22 December the last coach of the season goes down to Bannack with the camp's winter clean-up, $112,000 in dust; after it, the road closes until spring. Sefton means his gang to rob it below the ford, then burn Fiddler's Station with a murdered drifter inside so that the camp will mourn him, and take the cache over the pass into Idaho. The same night, in camp, Mordecai Pottinger and the last dozen of the committee mean to hang every name left on the list, starting with Davy Renner in the district jail; Sefton has seen to that too, because every eye in Ninebark will be on the corral and not the road, and because Davy is the witness who can hang him. The party has ten days to serve the warrants, find the cache and decide how to be in three places at once, and a blizzard is coming in on the 22nd. Then it is Christmas Eve, and whoever is left sits down in Moira Kehoe's parlour.
setting.atmosphere: The deep of winter. Snow every other day, the gulch half-buried, the creek silent under ice, the sun a pale disc that clears the ridge for four hours. Smoke stands straight up from the chimneys on still mornings and lies flat along the gulch before a storm. The road over the pass is a trench between drifts. On the 22nd the wind comes up at noon and the snow comes with it, and by dark it is a white roar in which a lantern cannot be seen at ten feet and a fire can be seen for miles. Christmas Eve is still and clear and bitterly cold, with stars over the gulch like frost.

keyLocations.name: Fiddler's Station
keyLocations.description: As before, but quieter. Sefton has sent the cook away for the winter. Jemmy the hostler is still there, and so, from 19 December, are two hired guns Sefton has brought up from the Beaverhead Crossing road, 'for protection, with all these road agents about'. A drifter called Shem Gorley, a broken-down prospector Sefton has taken in out of charity, sleeps in the barn and does odd jobs. Sefton means him to be the body in the fire.
features: The barn floor: at the back, under the feed sacks, a plank-lined pit four feet deep, empty now, with gold dust glittering in the cracks between the planks
Coal oil: six cans in the smithy shed, newly bought from Wexford's on Sefton's account, 'for the lamps'
The house: Sefton's room, his desk, his pencil, and a station register in the same round cramped hand as the twelfth name on the list
encounters: Warrick Sefton (Gang Leader, his Army Revolver read as a Navy revolver; he also carries a coach gun), two Hired Guns, and Jemmy
Shem Gorley, harmless, grateful, doomed if nobody notices
secrets: CLUE D6 (for anyone who searches the barn with a warrant or without one: Investigation DC 13, automatic if Davy Renner told them where): the pit under the barn floor, and the dust in its cracks.

The station register is in Sefton's hand: round, cramped, pressing hard enough to dent the page, and he writes 'federal' with an e in a note of 4 November: 'Mail lay over. Federel letter for agent.' Set beside the list, it is the pencil hand (CLUE C1 and E5, Investigation DC 11).

Jemmy, if anyone is gentle with him and promises him a ride out of the territory, tells everything he knows: the washing, the barn, the canyon, the coal oil, and that Mister Sefton told him to go to the Crossing on the 21st 'and not come back till Christmas'. He also knows Shem Gorley is to sleep in the house on the 22nd, 'because Mister Sefton says it's warmer'.

keyLocations.name: Deadfall Canyon
keyLocations.description: Two hours' ride west of Fiddler's by the gang's trail, which runs past the station's back corral; in December the trail is a trench, watched from the station, and nobody can use it unseen. There is another way in: from the top, down a snow-filled couloir from the ridge above the Upper Bench, which Chelo Arvizu found in 1863 looking for strayed mules. The canyon itself is a hidden meadow of winter grass with a spring that never freezes, a trapper's cabin of big logs, a brush corral, and the gang's horses.
features: The couloir: a steep chute of snow and rock, three hundred feet, with a cornice at the top; Survival DC 14 with Chelo Arvizu to find, Athletics DC 13 to descend, and a DC 14 DEX save for each climber if a cornice breaks
The cabin: bunks for six, a stove, rifles, and under the floor the cache: eleven buckskin pokes and a tin box, about $71,000 in dust from the first three robberies
A letter in the round, cramped hand, unsigned, tucked in a tobacco tin on the shelf
encounters: Judd Ferrier (Fast Gun, Army Revolver read as Navy), Wick Brill (Bandit Sharpshooter) and Hank Crewe (Outlaw), wintering in the cabin until the 21st, when they ride down to the station to get ready
A cougar that has been following the gang's horses (Cougar), if the GM wants the canyon to bite
secrets: CLUE E4 (core, in the tobacco tin): 'Last one Thursday 22nd. Below the ford, the Crossing road. Burn it after. Bring a man. Take the dust over Lemhi way, I will meet you at the forks.' In the hand of the pencil line on the list and the station register.

The cache is the robbers' downfall: it is the stolen dust, in the express company's own buckskin pokes with Prothero's seals still on some of them. Recovering it is worth $1,000 from the company and proves everything.

keyLocations.name: Below the ford: the Crossing road
keyLocations.description: Below the Rattlesnake Grade the road crosses the frozen creek and runs four miles down a narrow valley through willows and cottonwoods to the Beaverhead Crossing roadhouse. Halfway, the valley pinches between two red bluffs called the Gates. Sefton has moved the robbery here because every guard on the road watches the Elbow now. On the 22nd, with the blizzard coming, Ferrier, Brill, Crewe and the two hired guns wait in the willows at the Gates.
features: The Gates: two bluffs fifty feet high, a road between them twenty yards wide, willows on the creek side
The frozen creek, which will bear a man but not a coach
Visibility in the blizzard: 30 feet by 3 in the afternoon; ranged attacks beyond that at disadvantage, beyond 60 feet impossible
encounters: The last coach robbery, Thursday 22 December at about three in the afternoon (act 2)
secrets: If the party has the letter from Deadfall Canyon, they know the place and can be waiting for the waiters. If they have only the old pattern, they will guard the Elbow and the coach will be stopped at the Gates.

keyLocations.name: The district jail and the slaughter corral
keyLocations.description: Davy Renner is in the jail, the judge's prisoner now, bound over for the territorial court in the spring. Barnabas Wyndham keeps him, with the judge's warrant on the wall. On the night of the 22nd Pottinger and the last of the committee, a dozen men, mean to take him and anyone else on the list they can find and hang them at the corral, before the judge's court can do it 'too slow, or not at all'.
features: The jail door, with a new bar Gabriel Tennant forged for it
The corral gate, with the WARNED board still on it
In the blizzard, the lanterns can be seen only at thirty feet
encounters: Pottinger and eleven committee men (Lynch Mob at half strength, 30 hit points; Pottinger is the ringleader and unmasked now, because he no longer cares)
secrets: Sefton sent Pottinger a note on the 20th, by Nels Eklund if Eklund is free, or by a hired gun: 'They will let the boy go in the spring. The judge is soft. Thursday night, while the camp sleeps.' Pottinger does not know Sefton is a road agent, because he refuses to believe it. The note is in the round hand.

keyLocations.name: Moira Kehoe's parlour
keyLocations.description: Christmas Eve. The piano nobody can play. A tree cut from the hillside by Ada Brockway or the Number Three men, decorated with paper and candle-ends. Whoever is left.
features: The framed copy of Judge Marten's record clearing Patrick Kehoe, on the wall above the piano, if the party won it
A goose from Wexford's store, sent over without a bill

synopsis: With Judge Marten's warrants, the party can raise a posse and ride to Fiddler's Station. If Sefton has not been unmasked, he welcomes them with stew and an injured innocence, invites them to search, and laughs when the barn pit is empty: the dust went up to the canyon weeks ago. If he has been unmasked, the station is shut, two hired guns are on the porch, and Sefton talks through the door. Either way the proof is in Deadfall Canyon, and the only way into it unseen is from the top, down a snow-filled couloir that Chelo Arvizu knows. In the canyon the party can find the cache of stolen dust, $71,000 in the express company's own pokes, and a letter in the round hand of the pencil name on the list: the last coach, Thursday 22nd, below the ford; burn it after; bring a man. They may meet Ferrier, Brill and Crewe there, or find the cabin empty. On the 22nd, in a rising blizzard, three things happen at once. The last coach, with $112,000, is stopped at the Gates below the ford by Ferrier's gang. Fiddler's Station is set on fire with Shem Gorley, a harmless drifter, drugged inside it, so that the camp will think Sefton died. And in Ninebark, Pottinger's last dozen come for Davy Renner at the jail. The party has companions: Barnabas and Gabriel can hold the jail, Benicio and Cormac can ride the coach, Chelo can guide anyone anywhere; but they cannot be everywhere, and the players must choose. The reckoning is Sefton himself, caught on the pass road with the dust on pack mules, or at his burning station, or in Ninebark's street; he can be taken alive and brought to the judge, or killed in a showdown, or, if the party lets the committee have him, hanged at the gate by the men he used, which is a lynching all the same. Then the road closes, and on Christmas Eve the survivors sit down together in Moira Kehoe's parlour.
hook: Monday 12 December, the hotel dining room, the judge's warrants on the table in front of you, five of them, each with a name, a seal and the words 'robbery of the United States mails'. Barnabas Wyndham picks up the first one and reads the name on it twice, and puts it down, and takes off his spectacles. 'He gave me venison stew,' he says, 'every time I rode to Bannack. He wouldn't let me pay.' Outside the window it has begun to snow again. 'Ten days to the last coach,' says Simeon Prothero. 'And then the road closes, and whatever is gone is gone till spring.'

conclusions.conclusion: E. Warrick Sefton is the road agents' chief (proof for the court)
clues: D6: the pit under Fiddler's barn floor, with dust in the cracks (Fiddler's Station)
E4: the letter in the tobacco tin (Deadfall Canyon)
E5: the station register in the pencil hand, and Sefton himself (Fiddler's Station, the reckoning)
The cache in the express company's sealed pokes (Deadfall Canyon)

acts.title: Sunday to Wednesday: The Warrant and the Canyon
acts.description: The party serves the warrant at Fiddler's, and learns that the proof is somewhere else. Then they go to get it. The point of this act is the expedition into Deadfall Canyon from the top in deep winter, and the cache and letter at the end of it: the hard proof that ends the mystery and tells them where the last robbery will be.
objectives: Raise a posse and serve the judge's warrant at Fiddler's Station
Search the barn and the house, and find the pit and the register
Reach Deadfall Canyon unseen, with Chelo Arvizu, and recover the cache and the letter
encounters: At Fiddler's, if Sefton was unmasked: two Hired Guns on the porch and Sefton behind the door with a coach gun; he will not be taken, and will not fight a posse in daylight; he talks, stalls, and sends Jemmy out the back to warn the canyon

The couloir into Deadfall Canyon: Athletics DC 13 to descend, a cornice that may break (DC 14 DEX save, 2d6 bludgeoning and buried on a failure, DC 12 Athletics to dig out), and the cold (DC 15 CON save against exhaustion for a night out)
In the canyon before the 21st: Judd Ferrier (Fast Gun), Wick Brill (Bandit Sharpshooter) and Hank Crewe (Outlaw) in the cabin, with a cougar watching the horses

scenes.name: Fiddler's Station with a Warrant
scenes.description: If Sefton has not been unmasked, he comes out on the porch, reads the warrant with his spectacles on, laughs, and asks the posse in for stew. He invites them to search. He is sorrowful and wounded and entirely in control, and he knows the dust is in the canyon. The barn pit (CLUE D6) is empty, but the dust in its cracks is enough for any honest man, and the station register (CLUE E5) is in the pencil hand. He does not resist arrest, because he knows the judge needs more than an empty pit; and if the party arrests him anyway, he goes quietly to the Ninebark jail, and on the night of the 21st Ferrier's gang breaks him out (or the party must hold the jail against both the gang and the committee on the 22nd, which is a fine finale too). If he has been unmasked, the station is shut and guarded, and he talks through the door: reasonable, regretful, threatening. Either way, Jemmy is the key. Find him, be gentle, promise him a seat on a coach out of the territory, and he tells them everything, including the coal oil and Shem Gorley.
scenes.readAloud: He is on the porch before you have reached the corral, in his shirtsleeves in the snow, with a coffee pot in one hand, as if a posse of eight armed men were the best thing that had happened to him all week. He reads the warrant through, carefully, holding it at arm's length, and hands it back. 'Well,' he says. 'Well, well. That old man.' He shakes his head and laughs, and you would swear it is a real laugh. 'Come in, come in, it's bitter. Search where you like. Jemmy, put more meat in the pot. You'll find I've nothing to hide, friends, and when you've found it, we'll say no more about it.' Behind him, in the barn door, the thin hostler boy is looking at you, and then at the ground, and then at you again.

skillChecks.success: CLUE D6: the pit, and the glitter of dust between the planks, and the scrape-marks where something heavy was dragged out. And in the house, the register in the round, cramped hand: 'Federel letter for agent.'
skillChecks.failure: A barn, a house, a register. Sefton watches you search with sympathy.

skillChecks.success: Jemmy, alone, behind the smithy: everything, in a whisper. The washing. The barn. The canyon. 'He bought coal oil. Six cans. He told me to go to the Crossing on the twenty-first and not come back till Christmas. And Shem's to sleep in the house Thursday, because it's warmer.' The boy starts to shake. 'Shem's never slept in the house.'
skillChecks.failure: Jemmy shakes his head and runs back into the barn.

skillChecks.success: Sefton is not worried about the barn. He is worried about the canyon, and about the boy. He looks at Jemmy once, and you see him decide something.
skillChecks.failure: A cheerful man with nothing to hide.

scenes.name: Deadfall Canyon from the Top
scenes.description: Chelo Arvizu knows the way: up from the Upper Bench on snowshoes to the ridge, two hours, and down the couloir into the canyon's head, out of sight of the station and the gang's trail. It is the hardest physical challenge in the campaign: the cold, the snow, the cornice, the chute. Run it as a short series of checks with real consequences (exhaustion, a lost rifle, a twisted ankle) and let the companions shine: Chelo leading, Ada Brockway reading the snow, Gabriel Tennant hauling a rope. At the bottom, the canyon opens out: a white meadow, a dark cabin, smoke from the chimney if the gang is there, and horses in a brush corral.
scenes.readAloud: From the ridge the canyon is a long white bowl walled with black timber and grey rock, and at the bottom of it, so small you could cover it with your thumb, a cabin with a thread of smoke going straight up into the still air. Between you and it is the couloir: a steep chute of snow between two ribs of rock, falling away out of sight, with a lip of wind-packed snow curling over the top of it like a wave about to break. The packer woman stands at the edge of it on her snowshoes, looking down, with her serape pulled up over her nose. 'Last year I came down this after two mules,' she says. 'I got the mules. Walk where I walk. Don't stand on the lip.'

skillChecks.success: With Chelo, you find the safe line and the party descends without disturbing the cornice.
skillChecks.failure: Someone steps on the lip. It breaks. DC 14 DEX save for everyone in the chute; on a failure, 2d6 bludgeoning, buried, and a DC 12 Athletics check by someone else to dig them out.

skillChecks.success: Down the chute on the rope, in good order.
skillChecks.failure: A long, sliding fall at the bottom: 1d6 bludgeoning and a level of exhaustion.

skillChecks.success: You reach the meadow's edge unseen. If the gang is in the cabin, you have surprise.
skillChecks.failure: A horse in the corral whinnies. The cabin door opens.

scenes.name: The Cabin and the Cache
scenes.description: Before the 21st, Ferrier, Brill and Crewe are in the cabin; after it, the cabin is empty and the cache is still under the floor, because they will collect it on the way over the pass. A fight here is in the open snow against three hard men: Ferrier will not be taken alive if he can help it, Brill shoots from the doorway, Crewe tries for the horses. If the party takes Ferrier alive, he says nothing at all, then or ever. Under the cabin floor: the cache (eleven pokes, a tin box, about $71,000, Prothero's seals still on several pokes). On the shelf, in a tobacco tin: the letter (CLUE E4). Taking the cache changes the 22nd: Sefton's plan needs it, and he will come for it, or he will rob the last coach anyway and go without it.
scenes.readAloud: The cabin is warm, and smells of horse, tobacco, coffee and men who have not washed since October. Six bunks, a stove, a table with a deck of cards spread on it in a game of solitaire that somebody abandoned. Under the loose planks by the stove, wrapped in an old army blanket: buckskin pokes, eleven of them, heavy as lead for their size, and on four of them the little red wax seal of the Beaverhead Express Company with S.P. stamped in it. And on the shelf over the stove, in a tobacco tin, a folded sheet of paper, written in pencil in a round, cramped hand that presses so hard it has nearly gone through.

skillChecks.success: CLUE E4. 'Last one Thursday 22nd. Below the ford, the Crossing road. Burn it after. Bring a man. Take the dust over Lemhi way, I will meet you at the forks.' The same hand as the pencil line on the list.
skillChecks.failure: You find the cache. The letter you find only when you search the shelf, a minute later.

skillChecks.success: (If Ferrier is cornered.) He lowers his gun, slowly, and you see that he has decided to live. He will never testify, but he will hang by law in the spring, and he knows it.
skillChecks.failure: He makes his choice. Showdown (frontier.json showdowns): he will draw.

acts.title: Thursday 22 December: The Last Coach
acts.description: Three crises at once in a blizzard: the coach at the Gates, the fire at Fiddler's, the lanterns at the jail. The party cannot be everywhere. This is the act where the companions matter most: let the players assign them, and let them succeed or fail on the party's preparation. A party that has the letter, the posse and the judge's support can cover all three. A party that does not will have to choose, and something will be lost.
objectives: Bring the last coach through the Gates, or recover its boxes
Save Shem Gorley from the fire at Fiddler's
Hold the jail against Pottinger's last dozen without killing them
encounters: At the Gates, about three in the afternoon: Judd Ferrier (Fast Gun), Wick Brill (Bandit Sharpshooter), Hank Crewe (Outlaw) and two Hired Guns, minus anyone the party has already taken; in a blizzard (30 ft visibility)

At Fiddler's, about four: Sefton and Shem Gorley, drugged with laudanum in the house; coal oil; Sefton lights it and rides for the pass with the pack mules. The fire is a hazard: entering the burning house is a DC 13 CON save each round for 2d6 fire damage (half on a success); carrying Gorley out takes two rounds
At the jail, about nine at night: Pottinger and eleven men (Lynch Mob, 30 hit points), unmasked, with a rope; Barnabas Wyndham and Gabriel Tennant inside with Davy Renner

scenes.name: Who Goes Where
scenes.description: On the morning of the 22nd, with the sky going the colour of lead in the northwest, the party plans. Give them the facts they have earned and let them divide their forces. The coach must go; Prothero cannot hold $112,000 in a log vault through the winter and the miners will not let him try. Cormac Hartigan and Benicio Aranda (if played, or as NPCs) will ride it. Barnabas will hold the jail; Gabriel will stand with him. Chelo can take anyone over the ridge faster than the road. Konrad Kranzler or Moira Kehoe should be wherever someone will be hurt. If the party has Jemmy's word about Shem Gorley, someone must go to Fiddler's. If the party has the letter, they can ambush the ambushers at the Gates. If they took the cache, Sefton will come up the canyon trail for it, or abandon it. Whatever they decide, run the three scenes in order of time, cutting between them at moments of decision.
scenes.readAloud: By ten in the morning the wind has come up the gulch from the northwest, a long, low, steady push that makes the stovepipes hum, and the snow is coming with it: small, hard, dry flakes that hiss on the windows. Simeon Prothero stands at the door of the express office with his watch in his hand, looking at the green treasure boxes on the floor, four of them, and at the coach drawn up outside with its team stamping and blowing. 'A hundred and twelve thousand dollars,' he says. 'Everything this camp has dug since September. It goes today or it doesn't go till May.' He snaps the watch shut and looks at you. 'Where do you want your people?'

skillChecks.success: You see the shape of it: the coach is the bait, the fire is the getaway, the jail is the distraction. Sefton has put the camp's eyes on the corral and its guns on the road, and he will be on neither.
skillChecks.failure: Three dangers. Too few of you.

scenes.name: The Gates
scenes.description: Below the ford, in the blizzard, the road agents stop the coach at the Gates: a felled cottonwood across the road, Ferrier in front, Brill on the bluff, Crewe and the hired guns in the willows. Visibility is thirty feet. The fight is short, close and blind. If the party is waiting for the waiters (they have the letter), they have surprise. Ferrier fights to the end unless cornered; Brill surrenders if Ferrier falls; Crewe runs for the willows and the frozen creek, which may not bear him. A coach horse panicking in a blizzard between two bluffs is its own hazard.
scenes.readAloud: The world has shrunk to the coach and the horses and a few yards of white road and the black shapes of willows coming and going in the snow. The driver is singing to the team, something tuneless, to keep them steady. Then, very close, ahead, through the roar of the wind, somebody whistling. 'Aura Lea'. And a dark tangle across the road where no tree should be, and the leaders throwing up their heads, and a tall shape in a grey coat stepping out from the bluff into the coach lamps with a coach gun at his shoulder and no mask on at all this time, because it is the last time, and he does not care who sees.

skillChecks.success: In the blizzard, you see the man on the bluff before he fires.
skillChecks.failure: The first shot comes from somewhere above, out of the white.

skillChecks.success: You hold the team between the bluffs.
skillChecks.failure: The team bolts into the willows and the coach goes over on its side in the creek ice. Everyone inside makes a DC 13 DEX save or takes 2d6 bludgeoning.

scenes.name: Fire at Fiddler's
scenes.description: At about four, at Fiddler's Station, Warrick Sefton gives Shem Gorley a supper with laudanum in the coffee, lays him on the bed in the house, pours coal oil through the rooms, and sets it alight. Then he leads four pack mules out of the back corral and up the canyon trail toward the pass, meaning to collect the cache from the canyon and meet Ferrier at the forks beyond. If the party is there in time (they have Jemmy's warning), they can save Gorley and catch Sefton in the yard, or on the trail with the mules. If they arrive late, the house is a pillar of fire in the blizzard, visible for miles, and Gorley can still be saved with courage and a wet blanket; Sefton's tracks lead up the trail. If nobody comes, Gorley dies, and the camp believes for a week that Warrick Sefton died defending his station, and Barnabas Wyndham, of all people, gives the eulogy.
scenes.readAloud: You see it before you hear it: a glow in the snow ahead, orange, then red, then a column of light standing up into the storm where the station should be, with sparks streaming off it sideways in the wind. Then the sound, a roar like a furnace door opened, and under it, from the barn, the horses screaming. The house is burning from end to end. On the porch, in the doorway, black against the flames, there is something lying across the sill: a man, face down, one arm stretched out toward the snow, who got that far and no further.

skillChecks.success: You get him over your shoulder and through the smoke in two rounds (and make the CON save for each round inside, as the encounter says).
skillChecks.failure: He is a dead weight and the doorway is burning. Another round inside, another CON save, or let someone else try.

skillChecks.success: Laudanum, a great deal of it. Keep him awake, keep him walking. He lives.
skillChecks.failure: He is slipping away. Konrad Kranzler or Moira Kehoe can still save him (Sawbones).

skillChecks.success: Fresh tracks in the snow behind the barn: one man on foot leading four loaded mules, up the canyon trail toward the pass, not twenty minutes old.
skillChecks.failure: The snow is filling everything.

scenes.name: The Last Lanterns
scenes.description: At nine, in Ninebark, Pottinger and his last eleven come down Water Street through the blizzard for Davy Renner. Barnabas holds the door; Gabriel stands in front of it with his Bible; and whoever of the party is in camp is there too. This is the committee's last turnout, and it is small, unmasked and drunk. Mob Mind: Pottinger is unmasked already, so arresting him breaks it at once; Gabriel's Stand Between (if he has reached that level) or a Lawman's Stand Your Ground breaks it too. If the party can show Pottinger Sefton's note in the round hand, and the matching letter from the canyon, Pottinger understands at last who has been using him; the shock is an automatic success on any check against the mob, and he goes home and does not come out again. Nobody need die here. If Davy Renner is taken and hanged, the GM narrates it as what it is.
scenes.readAloud: They come down the street out of the snow with three lanterns between twelve of them, and no masks, and you know every face: the saloon keeper with his rosette, the foreman in the army overcoat, the grocer who went home from the widow's porch and has come back. They stop in front of the jail. The big Black blacksmith is standing in front of the door with a Bible in one hand and nothing in the other, and the snow is settling on his hat and his shoulders, and he does not move. 'Brother Pottinger,' he says, in a voice that carries over the wind. 'Go home. It's nearly Christmas. Go home.'

skillChecks.success: Mob Mind: 2d10 hit points of men turn and walk back up the street into the snow. With Sefton's note and the canyon letter shown to Pottinger: automatic, and the mob breaks.
skillChecks.failure: Pottinger shouts, and they come on.

skillChecks.success: A hand on Pottinger's collar and a star in his face: arrested, and the mob breaks at once.
skillChecks.failure: Somebody throws a lantern. It smashes on the porch and the coal oil catches.

acts.title: The Reckoning, and Christmas Eve
acts.description: Sefton, on the pass road in the storm with the dust on pack mules, or at the forks waiting for Ferrier, or, if the party took the cache, coming down into Deadfall Canyon for it. Wherever he is, the party finds him. He is not a gunfighter and he knows it; he talks first, and he talks well. Then Christmas Eve, the road closed, and whoever is left.
objectives: Take Warrick Sefton, alive if possible, and bring him to Judge Marten
Decide what to do if the committee demands him
Sit down together on Christmas Eve
encounters: Warrick Sefton (Gang Leader, his Army Revolver read as a Navy revolver, and a coach gun) with any surviving Hired Gun, on the pass road in the blizzard or at the canyon cabin; he will try to talk, then to buy, then to run, then to shoot

scenes.name: Sefton on the Pass
scenes.description: The party catches Sefton on the trail above the station with four mules loaded with dust (or at the canyon cabin, if they took the cache and he came for it). He stops, turns, and smiles. He offers them money, a share, $20,000 each, and means it. He offers them the truth: yes, he gave Tillery the names; yes, he added the marshal's; and the committee hanged them, not he, and every man on that committee will go home and sleep tonight. He asks them whether they are going to give him to the judge or to the committee, and watches their faces. If they refuse him, he tries to run with the mules (a chase in snow), and if cornered, he draws (frontier.json showdowns; he is a poor shot and knows it, and will try the stare-down first). Taken alive, he goes to Judge Marten and the jail, and talks pleasantly to Davy Renner through the bars about Kansas. Killed, he dies in the snow, still smiling. If the party hands him to the committee, or lets Pottinger's men take him from the jail on Christmas Eve, he is hanged at the corral by the men he used, and the GM narrates it as a lynching: it is not justice, it is the same crime again, and the camp never hears the whole truth in court.
scenes.readAloud: He has stopped in the lee of a rock where the trail tops the ridge, with the four mules standing head-down behind him, their packs white with snow, and he is waiting for you, sitting on a boulder with his coach gun across his knees and his hat pulled down and his collar up. When you are close enough to see his face he lifts a hand, as if he were on his porch and you were coming in off the road. 'Friends,' he says. 'Bitter weather. I've got coffee in the pack, and more dust on these mules than any of you will see in your lives, and I've been thinking that there's no reason on God's earth why we can't all of us be warm this winter.' He smiles. 'Unless you'd rather give me to the old man. Or to Mordecai and his rope. You'll have to choose, you know. Which is it to be?'

skillChecks.success: The offer is real, and so is the coach gun. He would pay you and then, one night in Idaho, he would shoot you, because you would know.
skillChecks.failure: He means it. Every word.

skillChecks.success: Stare-down won (frontier.json showdowns): he looks at you for a long time and then lays the coach gun in the snow. 'Well,' he says. 'Well, well.'
skillChecks.failure: He stands up, slowly, and the stare-down becomes a draw.

skillChecks.success: You tell him he is going to a court, and a jury, and the territorial judge in the spring, and that he will get what Jack Tillery did not. He laughs, and gives up, and for a moment he looks almost relieved.
skillChecks.failure: 'No,' he says, gently. 'I don't think so.'

scenes.name: The Sentinel's Extra
scenes.description: On Friday 23 December, Jonas Fenley prints a single sheet: the truth, as the examining court has heard it and the party has proved it, and, if the party gives it to him, the committee's roll. This is the party's choice, and a hard one: printing the roll names forty men, most of whom are frightened shopkeepers with families, and the camp will never be the same; not printing it lets them all go home. Either way the extra clears Patrick Kehoe, Tobiah Corder, Torvald Fjeld and every innocent name on the list, and announces that Warrick Sefton is in the district jail (or dead, or hanged by the committee, which Fenley will print as murder). Wexford, if turned, asks to have his own name printed first.
scenes.readAloud: The press in the back of the Sentinel's office is an old Washington hand press that came over the mountains in pieces on four mules, and the editor works it himself, in his shirtsleeves, with ink to the elbows, pulling one sheet at a time. He hands you the first one, still wet. EXTRA, it says. THE TRUTH OF THE ROBBERIES. WHO WROTE THE LIST. And below that, in smaller type: The citizens of Ninebark are informed that the names of the men hanged in this camp since the sixth of November were given by the robbers themselves. Fenley wipes his hands on a rag. 'There's room at the bottom,' he says, 'for the others. If you want them there.'

skillChecks.success: You persuade Fenley to print what you want and nothing you don't, and he does it gladly. It is the first thing he has printed since November that he is not ashamed of.
skillChecks.failure: He prints it, but he is frightened, and he leaves out the part about the committee.

scenes.name: Christmas Eve
scenes.description: Moira Kehoe's parlour, Saturday 24 December. The road is closed until spring. Whoever is left is here: the companions, the party, and whoever they saved. Barnabas Wyndham, if he lives, reads aloud from Luke, in Latin and then in English, badly. Gabriel Tennant leads a hymn. Chelo Arvizu brings a bottle of mescal she has been saving since Sonora. Leonie Fairbairn deals a hand of faro for matches. Moira hangs the judge's record on the wall above the piano. Torvald Fjeld, if he lives, tries to play the piano and cannot, and everyone laughs. Say who is there, and say whose names are not, and let the players end it.
scenes.readAloud: The snow stopped at dusk, and the sky over the gulch has cleared to a black so deep and cold that the stars look close enough to touch, and the whole camp is quiet, the kind of quiet that is not fear. In the widow's parlour there is a fir tree from the hillside hung with paper and candle-ends, a goose from Wexford's store that came without a bill, the piano that nobody can play, and as many chairs as the house has, and some borrowed. On the wall above the piano, in a frame Gabriel Tennant made from a horseshoe and a strip of tin, is a single sheet of paper in a court clerk's hand. The widow stands in front of it for a moment before she sits down. Then she turns round, and looks at all of you, and for the first time since you came to Ninebark, she smiles.

skillChecks.success: You play the piano that nobody can play. It is badly out of tune and you play it anyway, and the widow sings, in Irish, and nobody in the room will ever forget it.
skillChecks.failure: Nobody can play it. Everyone laughs, and that is better.

npcsInvolved.name: Warrick Sefton, 44
npcsInvolved.description: As before. On the 22nd he is calm, cheerful and ruthless, and at the end he is curious about what the party will choose.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get away rich; failing that, to make the party choose between the judge and the rope, and see which they pick.

npcsInvolved.name: Judd Ferrier, 36
npcsInvolved.role: Road agent; the killer of Will Danforth
npcsInvolved.description: As before. On the 22nd he wears no mask.

npcsInvolved.name: Wick Brill, 30
npcsInvolved.description: Squat, bearded, a Missouri bushwhacker in the war who never stopped; the man in the rocks above the Elbow. Surrenders if Ferrier falls.

npcsInvolved.name: Hank Crewe, 40
npcsInvolved.description: Big, slow, Davy Renner's cousin, who brought the boy into it and is sorry. Runs rather than fights.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get Davy out, which he cannot.

npcsInvolved.name: Jemmy, 16
npcsInvolved.description: As before. Promised a seat on a coach out of the territory, he tells everything.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get away from Fiddler's alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Shem Gorley, 60s
npcsInvolved.role: A broken-down prospector; the body Sefton needs
npcsInvolved.description: A gentle, toothless, grateful old man who has been prospecting since Sutter's Mill and found nothing, taken in by Sefton out of 'charity'. Sleeps in the barn. Thinks Sefton is the kindest man in the territory.
npcsInvolved.motivation: A warm place for the winter.

npcsInvolved.name: Mordecai Pottinger, 50
npcsInvolved.description: As before, unmasked, drunk, and down to eleven men.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To win one thing before it is over. He cannot.

npcsInvolved.name: Justice Elihu Marten, 60
npcsInvolved.description: As vg-scenario-003. Binds Sefton over for the territorial court in the spring, if he is brought in alive.

npcsInvolved.name: Fergal McGarvey, 50
npcsInvolved.role: Keeper of the Beaverhead Crossing roadhouse; name 8 on the list
npcsInvolved.description: A sour, honest, red-faced Ulsterman who wanted Sefton's station contract and told Prothero Fiddler's kept funny hours. Was right. His roadhouse is the nearest shelter to the Gates.

rewards.money: The Beaverhead Express Company pays its standing rewards: $500 for each road agent taken alive and delivered to the law, and $1,000 for the recovery of the stolen dust, plus $2,000 shared if the last coach reaches Bannack. The miners whose dust is recovered take up a subscription for the party, $1 an ounce, which comes to several hundred dollars. Sefton's offer of $20,000 each is real and is a crime to accept.
items: The cache of stolen dust, about $71,000, in the express company's pokes (to be returned)
The letter from the tobacco tin (CLUE E4)
Sefton's coach gun and his pencil
The Sentinel's extra, first sheet off the press
A place at the table in Moira Kehoe's parlour, every Christmas Eve, for as long as she keeps the house

twists: Sefton's last weapon is the choice. When the party catches him, he does not beg; he asks them whether they will give him to the judge or to the committee, and he genuinely wants to know. A party that hands him to Pottinger has done to him exactly what he did to Patrick Kehoe. Make sure the players feel the weight of that, and never narrate his hanging as satisfying: he dies as badly as the others did, and the camp never hears him answer in court.
Shem Gorley, saved, thinks Sefton is the kindest man in the territory, and cannot be made to believe otherwise. He brings Sefton tobacco in the jail every day until the spring.

If the party took Sefton to the jail before the 22nd, Ferrier's gang breaks him out on the night of the 21st with the hired guns, and the committee's last dozen arrive at the same jail the next night for Davy Renner. The party must hold one jail against both, which is a tighter, harder finale and a fine one.

Wexford, turned, insists on riding with the posse, and is useless with a gun, and stands in front of Sefton at the end and asks him why. Sefton tells him the truth: 'Because you let me, Obadiah. You all did. It was easy.'
dmTips: This is the finale. Budget an hour for the warrant and the canyon, two hours for the 22nd, and half an hour for the reckoning and the epilogue. If the table is short of time, combine the Gates and Fiddler's: the party catches Sefton at the burning station after saving Gorley, and the coach fights its own way through with Cormac and Benicio.

The three crises of the 22nd are a test of everything the party has built: witnesses, allies, evidence, the judge, the companions. Let preparation pay off. A party with the canyon letter, Jemmy's warning and a posse should be able to cover all three. A party without them should have to choose, and should lose something, and know what.

Never let the committee hang anyone in this scenario as a solution. If Pottinger's men take Davy Renner, or Sefton, it is a murder, and the epilogue should say so, and should say that the camp never spoke of it again.

Sefton is not a gunfighter. His showdown is a conversation with a gun in it. Let him talk; he is the best talker in the territory, and his last speech is the campaign's argument stated by the man who exploited it: that the committee did his killing for him because it was easy.
The epilogue is the campaign's last word. Name the empty chairs. If everyone lived, say so, and let it be warm.

Historical note for the GM: the real Montana committees went on hanging for years after 1864, and many of their members were honoured for it. This campaign is a fictional camp in which a few people decided otherwise, which also happened, more often than the histories remember.
